Chapter 9: Navigating Setbacks and Embracing Imperfection
No matter how carefully you plan, parenting always finds a way to surprise you. There are just some days when everything seems to go sideways—the baby won’t sleep, your toddler has a meltdown in the middle of the store, and all those good intentions you started with just seem to slip through your fingers. When that happens, it’s so easy to feel like you’re failing, isn’t it?
But here’s something interesting: in France, setbacks are seen in a whole different light. Mistakes aren’t signs that you’re not cut out for parenting—they’re just part of the process. Parents there tend to shrug, maybe even laugh, and then simply try again. There’s far less pressure to be perfect, and a lot more acceptance that family life is naturally a bit messy.
Let me share a quick story. Picture a rainy afternoon—a father’s watching his son stubbornly refuse a carefully prepared meal. Instead of turning it into a standoff, the dad just says, “You don’t have to eat it,” and leaves it at that. No drama, no fuss. And you know what? With the pressure off, the little boy eventually takes a bite on his own.
We don’t always realize how much energy goes into trying to control every outcome. But in France, there’s this willingness to let go a little—to trust that things will work themselves out. Kids are allowed to have bad days. And so are parents.
Here’s what stands out: embracing imperfection is actually freeing. When you stop chasing that impossible standard, you open up space for real joy, genuine connection, and growth together. Your family becomes a place where it’s okay to be human, flaws and all.
So here’s the takeaway: you don’t have to get everything right. What really matters is that you show up, do your best, and love your kids—through all the ups, downs, and everything in between.
